extracted.intended_audience: USPTO personnel (patent examiners, reexamination clerks, TC SPRE, SPE, OPLA)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidelines for USPTO examiners and clerks to handle ex parte reexamination requests, including interaction with federal court decisions, preparation of Notices of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificates (NIRC/PTOL-469), examiner’s amendments, claim-status designations, publication preparation, and related checklist items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely determination on reexamination requests and owner notification obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination on a request must be made within 3 months based on the record before the examiner without awaiting a Federal Court decision; the patent owner is required by 37 CFR 1.565(a) to promptly notify the Office of any prior or concurrent proceeding and of any Federal court decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because it is not realistic to predict issues a Federal Court will treat, the Office makes the determination without considering alleged court issues. If a court decision later issues, the request will be reviewed per the guidelines. The patent owner has an affirmative duty to promptly notify the Office that a decision has been issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Federal court decisions on reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-final federal court decisions have no binding effect on reexamination; final decisions upholding validity are not binding but may be given deference; a final holding of invalidity or unenforceability (after all appeals) is binding on the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethicon v. Quigg: Office uses a different standard (preponderance) than district courts (clear and convincing), so the Office is not bound by a court's validity holding; factual findings of a court will ordinarily be accorded deference when evidence is the same. If a claim is finally held invalid/unenforceable, it will be withdrawn from reexamination consideration; reexamination continues as to remaining claims. If all claims are finally held invalid/unenforceable, the TC Director will vacate the reexamination as no longer containing a substantial new question of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 22.20 for claims held invalid by court
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 22.20 at the beginning of an Office action when claims are held invalid by a court and thus are no longer being reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paragraph includes bracketed insertions: bracket 1 for claim(s) held invalid, bracket 2 for patentee name, bracket 3 for the decision citation, bracket 4 for the court name. Follow the examiner note instructions when completing the paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner reasonable investigation for litigation involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must conduct a reasonable investigation to determine whether the patent has been or is involved in litigation, including review of the reexamination file, patent file, and litigation computer search results by the STIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If litigation or a federal court decision is discovered at any time during reexamination, the examiner must bring the fact to the attention of the TC SPRE prior to further action so the TC SPRE can ensure Office litigation policy and guidelines are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal court decisions controlling as to claims finally held invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a federal court has ruled and ex parte reexamination remains appropriate, the federal court decision will be followed and considered controlling as to claims finally held invalid by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This control applies only to claims finally held invalid; other claims remain subject to reexamination as appropriate per the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC/PTOL-469)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon conclusion of the reexamination proceeding, the examiner must prepare an NIRC (form PTOL-469), and if appropriate, an examiner’s amendment; where claims are found patentable, reasons must be given for each patentable claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the reexamination file for publication so the Office of Publications can issue a certificate per 35 U.S.C. 307 and 37 CFR 1.570. See MPEP § 2288 for details. If examiner intends to find claims patentable, notify SPE to convene a patentability review conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability review conference requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner intends to find any claim(s) patentable (confirmed or allowed) in concluding the reexamination, the examiner informs their SPE who convenes a patentability review conference; the conferees review the patentability and will initial the NIRC if confirmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two conferees must initial the NIRC to indicate participation; both initial even if one dissents. Exceptions: no conference where the claim was in the case when reviewed by the Board or a federal court; no conference when proceeding is concluded by cancellation of all claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRC effects and post-termination filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A NIRC informs the patent owner and requester that reexamination prosecution has been terminated; rules do not provide for an amendment after prosecution termination—such filings must be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisions of 37 CFR 1.312 do not apply in reexamination. Any amendment, IDS, or other merit-related paper filed after prosecution termination requires a petition under 1.182.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing the title or abstract during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Title changes generally not needed; if a title change is necessary the patent owner should be notified to provide an amendment early; if all claims are patentable and a NIRC is to be mailed, the examiner may change the title only by an examiner’s amendment (not by mere initialing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner’s amendment can change the abstract when the narrowing amendments during reexamination change the invention's focus (e.g., claim narrowed and abstract no longer focuses on required limitation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of representative claim(s) and drawing for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Select an appropriate drawing figure and a representative claim to be printed in the Official Gazette; reexamination instructions for claim selection: (A) select the broadest claim; (B) ordinarily designate only one claim per invention—reexamination: select only one claim; (C) do not select a dependent claim unless its independent claim is also printed (with reexamination exceptions); (D) in reissue, select the broadest claim with changes or broadest reissue claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recording, write claim numbers in black ink, separate multiple claims by commas, and refer to renumbered patent claim numbers (not original application numbers). In reexamination a dependent patent claim may be selected where the independent original claim was canceled (dependent printed while independent not printed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing attorney/agent names on certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner desires attorney/agent or firm names printed on the certificate, a separate paper limited to this issue listing the names and positively stating they should be printed must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere power of attorney or change of address is not a sufficient request for printing names on the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner completion of PTO-1516 and review of title report
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must complete checklist form PTO-1516 identifying information used for printing the reexamination certificate and should inspect the title report/patent abstract of title in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If title report indicates title in inventors but patent copy shows assignment to assignee, examiner may telephone patent owner and request a statement under 37 CFR 3.73(b) indicating title is in the assignee. PTO-1516 is forwarded to the Office of Publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination clerk duties and PTO-1517
rubrics_metrics.description: After examiner prepares NIRC and attachments and completes PTO-1516, the reexamination clerk completes PTO-1517, revises/updates files, and checks for proper entry of changes (title, inventor, assignee, continuing data, foreign priority, attorney address, requester address) in the IFW and PALM database before forwarding to TC SPRE and OPLA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerk should personally review the file before completing items; after TC SPRE approval the clerk mails the NIRC and forwards the proceeding to OPLA for ultimate publication processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when all claims are canceled
rubrics_metrics.description: If all claims in the reexamination are to be canceled (e.g., patent owner failed to respond or Board affirmed rejections and appeal time expired), the examiner should telephone the patent owner to confirm no timely filing; if none, issue a NIRC terminating prosecution and attach an examiner’s amendment canceling all live claims with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of explanatory statements are provided (failure to respond citing 37 CFR 1.550(d) and MPEP § 2266, or Board decision and no timely appeal). If a telephone interview is made, make it of record. Physically cancel live claims by bracketing on a claims copy and scanning into IFW. Designate a cancelled original patent claim for printing in Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of multiple dependent claims for NIRC and checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: For NIRC purposes, addition of a claim of multiple dependency is viewed as adding a new claim; deletion is viewed as canceling that dependent claim; change in chain of dependencies may designate claims as confirmed, amended, new, or canceled as appropriate for the NIRC and Examiner’s checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed examples illustrate designation: when a multiple dependency is added referencing a new claim, that dependent is treated as a new claim (e.g., 2/8); deletion of a dependency cancels the dependent claim (e.g., 3/1 canceled); addition/deletion for Examiner’s checklist often treated as amendment because of printing conventions. Ensure accurate mapping between pre- and post-reexamination protected subject matter and checklist entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminders — all claims must be examined
rubrics_metrics.description: All patent claims must have been examined in the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2243 for examination requirements; ensure no claims left unexamined before concluding the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminders — no renumbering of patent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: No renumbering of patent claims is permitted; new claims may require renumbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2250 for rules on claim numbering and renumbering in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminders — amendments conform to 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j)
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the description and claims must conform to the requirements of 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), including examiner’s amendments; if a portion of the text is amended more than once, each amendment should indicate all changes (insertions and deletions) relative to current patent text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2250 for formatting and marking conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminders — prior art listing forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art must be listed on an approved form (PTO-892, PTO-1449, PTO/SB/08A or 08B, PTO/SB/42, or an equivalent format); these forms must be properly completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2257 for prior art listing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminders — completion and agreement of checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner and reexamination clerk checklists (PTO-1516 and PTO-1517) must be entirely and properly completed; the reexamination clerk should personally review the file and ensure related items on both checklists agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerical checklist is designed to check the examiner’s responses; careful reading of checklist instructions is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminders — merge multiple pending reexaminations
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple pending reexamination proceedings must be merged when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2283 for merger procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminders — handling copending reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reexamination is copending with a reissue application for the patent being reexamined, files must be forwarded to OPLA for consideration of potential merger, with a decision by a Senior Legal Advisor or Special Projects Examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2285 for guidance on evaluating merger potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminders — reasons required for each claim found patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for patentability and/or confirmation are required for each claim found patentable (unless all claims canceled); the examiner should indicate why claims are clearly patentable over cited patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons may be set forth on form PTOL-476 or by using form paragraph 22.16 (preferred). Where the record clearly establishes patentability, the examiner may refer to specific record portions. Box 2 of PTOL-469 is checked and reasons attached. Patent owner comments on the reasons will be placed in the reexamination file without comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminders — no issue fee; amendments after patent expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no issue fee in reexamination; patent claims may not be amended nor new claims added after expiration of the patent. If the patent has expired, all amendments and claims added during the proceeding must be withdrawn, and presently rejected/objected-to claims are canceled by examiner’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2233 and § 2250 (part III) for details on amendment after patent expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminders — original drawings and scope of amended/new claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Original drawings cannot be physically changed; all drawing amendments must be presented on new sheets. An amended or new claim may not enlarge the scope of the patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A draftsperson’s approval stamp is no longer required. Examiner may have draftsperson review new sheets to identify errors. See MPEP § 2250.01 and § 2250.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendment requirements in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner makes amendments (or requests the patent owner to provide them), examiner’s amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j). Full text of any paragraph or claim to be changed must be presented with 1.530(f) markings; the exception allowing deletion by statement permits deletion of an entire claim or entire paragraph without presenting the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception for examiner’s amendments in 37 CFR 1.121(g) does not apply in reexamination. When an examiner’s amendment is prepared, check Box 7 of PTOL-469 and use form paragraph 22.06 to provide attachments and indicate the changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 22.06 — Examiner’s Amendment accompanying NIRC
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.06 is the examiner’s amendment wording to be used as an attachment to the NIRC indicating the changes made by the examiner’s amendment will be reflected in the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paragraph 22.06 as the attachment; include the changes (bracketed text) and ensure the examiner’s amendment markings comply with 37 CFR 1.530.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for patentability and/or confirmation content and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for patentability must be provided (unless all claims canceled), typically as an attachment to Box 2 of PTOL-469, indicating why the claims found patentable are clearly patentable over cited patents/printed publications; examiner may use PTOL-476 or form paragraph 22.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may refer to record portions which establish patentability. The terms 'confirmed' and 'patentable' may be used flexibly; no need to separate categories in the reasons. Any comments from patent owner about the reasons will be placed in the reexamination file without comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance and content of ex parte reexamination certificate (35 U.S.C. 307; 37 CFR 1.570)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon conclusion of ex parte reexamination and expiration/termination of appeals, the Director will issue and publish a certificate canceling any claim finally determined unpatentable, confirming any claim determined patentable, and incorporating proposed amended or new claims determined patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ex parte reexamination certificate will be issued for each patent where reexamination was ordered and not merged with an inter partes reexamination. Statutory disclaimers will be made part of the certificate. The certificate will be mailed to the patent owner and a copy to the requester on its date. If all claims are canceled, no further Office proceedings on that patent or related reissue/reexamination requests will be conducted. If terminated by grant of a reissued patent under § 1.565(d), the reissued patent constitutes the reexamination certificate.
